claims.summary: For every prime p, on near-permutations (one doubled hole) and on one-empty-pigeon assignments of unary PHP^{n+1}_n, plain or functional, a linear decision tree over F_p of depth O(log n) finds a falsified clause, by counting pigeons in hole sets or holes of pigeon sets; so the known hard distributions of the bounded-depth closure method (Byramji-Impagliazzo Remark A.4 at p=2) are easy at every prime. claims.summary: Column dichotomy for unary PHP^{n+1}_n on any bipartite graph G, any prime p: for a hole set H_0 with |H_0| >= n/2, if the systems {occupancy(h) = 1 mod p for h in H'}, over uniform r_0-subsets H' of H_0, hold with average probability at most delta, then for every eta in (0,1) a linear decision tree over F_p of depth O(r_0 log(2/eta)(log n + log(2/eta))) finds a falsified hole clause with probability at least 1 - 4 delta/3 - eta; boards without a matching covering n/2 holes are easy outright. So the closure method's probability property, if it charges these safe column systems, contradicts its distributional search hardness for every distribution on every board. Exempting the occupancy forms as Byramji-Impagliazzo Lemma 5.7 exempts column sums is blocked by safety: beside the n-p+1 fixed occupancy forms of the modular-collision distribution, a safe system has at most p further independent forms.
claims.assessment: Working proof of the Proposition (elementary: counting visible holes, sampling a pigeon, modular subset tests), checked by a fresh-context reviewer. Its consequence for the bounded-depth closure line: the probability property fails as charged, and a column-exempt version would need a new danger notion and closure lemma, which neither the record nor the cited sources have.

claims.summary: For unary PHP over F_p, p odd, the rank-one system x_{1a}+x_{2a}+x_{3a} = 2 (with occupancy equations, a having at least p further neighbours) forces a collision in hole a without forcing any cell, so closures defined by forced cells (one-shot, or iterated with matching propagation) fail the Efremenko-Garlik-Itsykson Delayer step at rank at most two. Any local-consistency notion requiring a 0/1 solution, monotone under implication over 0/1 points, with the leaf property and the Delayer step below rank m, must reject every system on m cells whose 0/1 solutions all collide there; for p >= 5 one equation can spread such collisions over p-2 holes, so a closure seeing them needs at least p-2 rows and holes.
claims.assessment: Counterexample and necessary condition with complete elementary proofs, checked by a fresh-context reviewer. Refutes the forced-cell candidate of the closure route review; the extendability closure remains open.

claims.summary: For plain unary PHP on a bipartite graph over F_p: call a subspace U of forms theta-dangerous when the vertex-cover number of its support (rows and holes) is below theta dim U; a greedy closure adding minimum covers strictly decreases |S| + theta dim<F[\S]>, so it has size at most theta rank (O(p r log r) with the theta that the onto lemma needs). Local consistency (an existential witness S within a budget with F[\S] theta-safe and a 0/1 solution injective on S, trapped pigeons included) has the leaf property and weakening under span containment, and rejects the forced-collision examples. Its Delayer step through the greedy continuation is refuted: hole covers trap pigeons (x_{as1}+x_{cs1}=1, x_{bs2}+x_{ds2}=1, f = x_{kh}+x_{k'h}); expansion and a cover-choice rule are needed. No least closing set exists (x_{1a}+...+x_{ma}); for functional PHP one row-count equation needs a closure of |R| rows.

claims.summary: For plain unary PHP over F_p with occupancy equations col_h = 1 imposed on local consistency: measure danger of a subspace modulo the occupancy span W by the least cover number of a representative (theta-dangerous when below theta times the quotient dimension). The greedy closure strictly decreases |S| + theta dim(<F[\S]>+W_S)/W_S, so |S| <= theta times the rank modulo W; occupancy forms (block column sums included) are exempted without the safety cap of pigeon-row safety; with absorbed cells (a cell whose column is otherwise pinned) trapping pigeons, the empty system is locally consistent and the negations of hole and pigeon clauses are not; the forced-collision examples are rejected (the calibration family for theta > p-2); and if the system is safe modulo W with theta >= 2l and every hole keeps at least 2l free cells, the occupancy equations join the onto lemma. The Delayer step and the treatment of row sums remain open.

claims.summary: Two closures for plain unary PHP over F_p fail the Delayer step on the full board. Private holes: with k = ceil(theta) and 2k+p <= n, Phi = {x_{i h_i} = 1 (i <= k), sum_i x_{j_i h_i} = 1} has a collision in every 0/1 solution, yet the vertex-cover closure (with or without the occupancy quotient) accepts it with witness the rows 1..k, since a closure pigeon's hole may hold other pigeons; by the rejection argument some query on a locally consistent system of rank at most 2k has no locally consistent answer, for every budget >= k and every theta > 1 in range. Row sums: a closure by matching edges (each closure pigeon in exactly one hole) accepts {sum_{i in R} row_i = v} with |R| = ceil(theta), v != |R| mod p, n >= max(2|R|, p), but no answer to row_{i_1} is locally consistent (rank two).
claims.assessment: Counterexamples with complete elementary proofs, checked by a fresh-context reviewer. They refute the Delayer step of prop:unary-vertex-cover-closure and prop:unary-closure-modulo-occupancy, and of a matching-edge variant; they motivate the star closure of prop:unary-star-closure-delayer-step.

claims.summary: Over F_p, let Psi be affine equations in the cells of a bipartite graph between pigeons and holes in which every hole has a neighbour, W the span of the column forms and O' = {col_h = 1}. If Psi together with O' is consistent over F_p and <Psi> is theta-safe modulo W (least cover number of a representative at least theta times the quotient dimension), with theta >= l_q for the quotient rank q (the Alon-Linial-Meshulam number: (1-1/p)^(l-p+2) q < 1), then for every map d choosing a neighbour d(h) of each hole there is a 0/1 solution of Psi and O' with exactly one pigeon in every hole, equal to d(h) for all but at most l_q q holes. Proof: Edmonds' matroid intersection of the l_q-fold union of the switch-vector matroid with the column partition matroid, safety bounding the number of non-constant columns, then ALM Proposition 3.1.
claims.assessment: Working proof from imported theorems (Edmonds' intersection theorem, the Nash-Williams union rank formula, Alon-Linial-Meshulam Proposition 3.1), checked by a fresh-context reviewer; the extension from the complete board to bipartite graphs is the reviewer's remark, checked by the author.

claims.summary: Star closure for plain unary PHP on the full board over F_p (danger modulo the occupancy span, occupancy equations imposed): a witness is a set of closure pigeons, closure holes and an owner map, not necessarily onto; its pattern puts each closure pigeon exactly in its owned holes and each closure hole's only pigeon is its owner. With theta > 1: negated hole clauses are not locally consistent; negated pigeon clauses are (a closure pigeon may own nothing), but no system of rank below n/(p-1) with a 0/1 solution implies one (Olson). With theta >= l_r and rank at most r: locally consistent systems have a 0/1 solution with one pigeon per hole, and the Delayer step holds in one-node form: extending the closure greedily by the stars of a solution from lem:Fp-safe-forms-one-pigeon-per-hole gives alpha and sigma* with |sigma*| + 3 theta D* <= |sigma| + 3 theta (D+1) + l_r D. Along a single path the Delayer can keep one near-matching and the closure is at most 2 theta T after T queries, so the content is the one-node form.
claims.assessment: Working proofs, checked by a fresh-context reviewer, whose correction (the path form is easy, with a linear budget) is recorded. Not a closure theory for the random walk: no canonical closure, no pigeon-clause leaf, possibly quadratic budget along paths that re-choose the solution, and no hard distribution.

claims.summary: For the modular-collision near-bijection mu_E on unary PHP over F_p (p >= 3: n+1 pigeons onto the holes outside a fixed set E of p-1 holes, one hole h* receiving p+1 pigeons): queries constant on the support are exactly those additive on pigeons x (holes outside E); (1) if the cells are partitioned among k players, integer sums of hole labels give an O(k log n)-bit protocol finding two colliding pigeons, so communication bounds through simulations where players hold cells give at most d = O(log n / log p) for linear trees (lifted simulations are not covered); (2) K = O(log n) fixed rank-one queries separate every support point from each of its single swaps (p >= 3), so single-swap sensitivity arguments give at most O(log n). No linear tree faster than sampling (about (n/p) log_p(n/p) queries) was found.
claims.assessment: Working proofs of the two obstructions (elementary), checked by a fresh-context reviewer; the absence of a fast tree is evidence, not a theorem. Search hardness of mu_E was later proved up to depth about n^{1/3} (thm:modular-collision-linear-search-hardness).

claims.summary: Two simulation lemmas for unary queries over F_p. L1 (easy direction of the standard four-point test): if a matrix C is at distance dist(C) from additive matrices a_i + b_h, a random swap of two pigeons' holes changes Q_C = sum_i C(i, g(i)) with probability at least dist(C), for independent or bijective choices and, under mu_E, at least (1 - O(p^2/m^2)) dist(C). L2: for independent uniform bits and nonzero differences delta_k in F_p, |Pr[sum delta_k beta_k = v] - 1/p| <= ((p-1)/p) cos(pi/p)^t <= exp(-pi^2 t / (2 p^2)); if every delta_k = +-1 (rectangle queries) the maximal deviation is at least (sqrt 2 / p) cos(pi/p)^t, so about p^2 log(1/eta) swaps are needed; one swap gives only two values, so Byramji-Impagliazzo's one-bit localization does not transfer to odd p.
claims.assessment: Working proofs (elementary counting and Fourier analysis), checked by a fresh-context reviewer, whose mu_E version of L1 and lower bound in L2 were checked by the author. L1 is standard.

claims.summary: The marginal-bounds lemma: let G be a bipartite graph between pigeons A and holes B, |A| = |B| + p, in which every pigeon misses at most mu holes and every hole misses at most mu' pigeons, and nu_G the uniform law on maps g into G with one hole h* receiving p+1 pigeons (the set S*) and every other hole one. With b = |B| and F_1 = b - mu - mu' - 1: nu_G(g(i)=h, h regular) <= 1/F_1; nu_G(i in S*) <= (p+1)/F_1; nu_G(i, i' both in S*) <= p(p+1)/F_1^2; nu_G(h* = h) <= p! b^p / ((b-1) F_2^p) with F_2 = F_1 - p; and nu_G(g(i)=h, h regular) >= F_3 (1 - theta)/((b-1)(b-2)) for every edge, with F_3 = F_1 - 2 and theta = (2p+3)/F_1 + p! b^p/((b-1)F_2^p), hence pair marginals of order 1/b^2.

claims.summary: The graph swap-test lemma: if every pigeon misses fewer than |B|/3 holes of a bipartite graph G, every function C on the edges at distance dist from the additive functions a_i + b_h has alternating sum nonzero on at least a fraction dist/K of the 4-cycles of G, with K = (b(a-1)/((a-mu')(b-mu)))(1 + 3b/(b-3mu))(b/(b-2mu))^2 (K <= 7.3 when mu <= b/15, mu' <= a/15); in particular 4-cycle-invariant functions are additive. Example H: on the blow-up of the 6-cycle (each vertex adjacent to two of three classes) the function 1 on A_1 x B_2 is invisible to every 4-cycle, not additive, and its query is not constant on the support of nu_G (finite check: all values mod 3). Under nu_G with missing bounds <= b/15, a uniform pair of pigeons gives a detecting swap with probability at least dist/15.
claims.assessment: Working proof (plurality decoding with a cocycle check on triple neighbourhoods), checked by a fresh-context reviewer; the exact version and Example H confirmed by a finite check (72 random dense graphs, 3 blow-ups).

claims.summary: The modular-collision theorem: for every odd prime p there are C_p, n_p such that for n >= n_p every linear decision tree over F_p (arbitrary affine queries in the variables x_{ih} of unary PHP with n+1 pigeons and n holes) of depth d that outputs two pigeons outputs two pigeons of one hole under the modular-collision near-bijection mu_E (n+1 pigeons onto the holes outside a fixed set E of p-1 holes, one hole receiving p+1) with probability at most C_p d sqrt((d + ln n)/n); so depth Omega_p(n^{1/3}) is needed for success probability 1/2. Proof: swap simulation in dense graphs; combinations of queries close to additive are made additive by revealing the pigeons on their exceptional cells, the others are localized on fresh random pairs whose orientations are hidden uniform bits (Fourier bound for systems), with a transfer from the prior along fixed paths to the adaptive tree.
claims.assessment: Working proof, checked by a fresh-context reviewer. Search hardness only: the random walk of Byramji and Impagliazzo also needs a probability bound and a restriction. Novelty not checked.

claims.summary: The detecting-swaps lemma: for a dense class (fixed pigeons sent to distinct holes of H', and a remaining graph G' between A' and B' = H' minus those holes, |A'| = |B'| + p, such that G' and every G'-i-h satisfy the hypotheses of lem:near-bijection-dense-marginals with F_3 > 0 and theta < 1, every pigeon missing fewer than |B'|/3 holes; the class is all maps extending the fixed pigeons with the rest in the support of nu_{G'}): if L = a holds on the class, the coefficient matrix of L is additive on G'; if L != a holds on the class, no map has p-1 pairwise disjoint swaps changing L, and in the regime of the modular-collision theorem L is within 4(p-2)K_0/|A'| of additive on G' (K_0 <= 15). Hence, in that regime, a class implying an equation or inequation at distance eps from additive on the full board fixes at least eps m/4 pigeons or deletes about eps n m/2 cells.

claims.summary: The bounded-degree head-count lemma: let delta >= 2 and k <= s/4 and let H be q distinct subsets of [s] of sizes 1..delta (heads); with E the delta-sets containing a head and theta = |E|/C(s,delta) (theta >= q/(2^delta C(s,delta)), equality without 2^delta for delta-uniform heads), the number of subsets of [s] of size at most k containing no head is at most sum_{j<delta} C(s,j) + 2.3 C(s,k) exp(k(delta-1)/s - k theta/delta). Proof by Lovasz's form of Kruskal-Katona. For the kernel method's dense step at p >= 5 (delta = p-1, s = 15(N+1), k = ceil(sqrt(N Lambda))) it gives a threshold Q_*^(p) = O_p(N^(p-3/2) sqrt(log N)) of distinct heads, against Theta_p(N^(p-1)) possible; at delta = 2 it sharpens (DH-count).

claims.summary: The all-prime graph criterion: for every odd prime p (delta = p-1), a polynomial inventory and sufficiently large N, on the separated sixteen-neighbor graph with s = 15(N+1) projected coordinates, a source of M complete accuracy-one blocks with old inputs of degree at most delta (all companions and coefficient fields) has no ordinary PC refutation through D >= 2p-1 when every block's nonlinear rank r_a in P_{<=delta}/I_delta(Gamma_H) modulo affine is at most R or at least Q_*^(p) = ceil(2^delta delta C(s,delta)((delta-1)/s + 5k/N + (Lambda+1)/k)), with Lambda = log(64(M+1)), k = ceil(sqrt(N Lambda)), T = (p-1)(H_* + delta R) + p and TD + k <= N/10^6 (so RD <= c_p N: R <= N^sigma polylog N for polylog D, R <= c_p N for bounded D). Q_*^(p) = O_p(N^(p-3/2) sqrt(log N)); at p = 3 it is the ternary criterion up to constants.

claims.summary: The all-prime clique-head theorem: under the hypotheses of thm:allprime-low-or-dense-graph-rank-exclusion, blocks satisfying (CH_delta-hyp) for some coordinate set M of size m_*^(p) = ceil((2s/k)(5k^2/N + Lambda + log(C_delta/2))) = O_p(sqrt(N log N)) also join the criterion, where (CH_delta-hyp) asks that every delta-subset of M be a leading monomial of span(inputs) + projected old ideal under the degree-then-M-weight-then-lex order. Lemma CH_delta: a head family containing all delta-subsets of an m-set leaves at most 2 C_delta binom(s,k) exp(-mk/(2s)) sets of size at most k free, with C_delta = (4(delta-1))^(delta-1) e^(1/4-(delta-1)). Random dense blocks with h >= (binom(m,delta) ln p + Lambda)/ln(1/eps_p) inputs satisfy it, eps_p = 1-(1-1/p)^delta, so the threshold for them is Theta_p((N log N)^((p-1)/2)) instead of N^(p-3/2).
claims.assessment: Working proof, transcribing the ternary clique-head refinement; checked by a fresh-context reviewer. The random-block count uses a multilinear Schwartz-Zippel bound and a plain union bound, weaker in constants than the ternary stratified count. The old relations alone cannot satisfy the hypothesis, so a block whose input span has dimension below (2s/k) log(8(M+1)) = O_p(sqrt(N log N)) never does; whether large structured common-factor blocks such as the sunflower family satisfy it is not decided, since their inputs give no coefficient on the relevant delta-subsets but cancellation against the old relations is not excluded. The window stays open at every prime.

claims.summary: Top-size lemma: a normalized mixture of pulled-back restriction designs annihilating U, where all components at sizes outside a set I annihilate U and I meets the nonzero-weight sizes only at the largest one, has a normalized sub-mixture on I annihilating U. Applied, under typicality hypothesis (T), to the ternary endpoint designs and an inventory with n random tuples at every input count: every successful PC mixture contains a degree-D PC design for the old base plus the n tuples of one input count, built from components not required to handle them.
claims.assessment: The lemma is elementary linear algebra with a complete proof; the application is conditional on (T), dense-side rank preservation at every restriction the mixture uses, which has no union bound for families chosen after the inventory. A reduction of the sheaf-entry mixture lead to a one-count design problem, not a refutation of mixtures; the one-count problem is a special case of the window problem and may be easier.

formalization.scope: Informal elementary lemma and conditional application; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Parks the last gluing lead of the odd-prime window behind a one-count design problem: restriction mixtures cannot use the sizes where window blocks are easy to supply the normalization.
significance.next_action: Reopen restriction mixtures only with a mechanism for a PC design of the old base plus many random window tuples of one input count.

claims.summary: Wide-conditioning conjecture: for each odd p and D there are t,Q such that ordinary unary PHP plus an affine system with linear parts independent modulo rows, every nonzero combination Q-robust on at least t rows, has no degree-D PC refutation. With the transversal special case of the constant-row clamp, a transversal meeting it excludes a compiled source; but any width-t span has dimension at most (N+2-t)(N-1) < N^2, so for about that many random blocks or more no transversal meets the hypothesis. Control: C_j=1 for j<N has width N+1 but a degree-two refutation, so robustness is needed.
claims.assessment: Conjecture, untested beyond its recorded one-form and two-form special cases at their own parameters; the r-parameter lift it needs is unproved and the projective proof does not port. The dimension bound and union bound are proved, and the control is a checked hand refutation. The ceiling limits the conjectured sufficient condition, not transversal or other constant-substitution designs.

formalization.scope: Informal conjecture, counting bound and hand control; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: States the natural many-form extension of the p-complex lifts; if true it would give quadratic reach for common affine conditioning, beyond the recorded linear endpoints, while its width hypothesis cannot reach polynomially many random window blocks.
significance.next_action: Test the conjecture at constant degree on small robust systems of rank above the one- and two-form cases, or prove an r-parameter lift; it does not by itself address the window.

relationships.note: Special case of the constant-row clamp for its reduction; generalizes the one-predicate conditioned filtration; answers the three-selector control's scope by moving to existence. Random affine conditioning check: with t=2D+1 the width hypothesis fails an O(D log n) term before hardness in random systems. Symmetric-lift entry: the r-parameter lift it needs holds only for symmetric targets, and on the matching complex only if a degree-window Ext vanishing holds. Density-principle entry: one constraint reduces to wide conditioning of its patterns; the Boolean-image control shows robustness is needed at density below one. Freeness-line review: the truncated Dade lemma is a column-tensor analogue of its r-parameter lift; that analogue fails without genericity. Column-type affine entry: occupancy systems meet its robustness hypothesis and are refuted at degree three for small Q at n = 6, 7. Occupancy witness entry: freeness-based proofs need Q >= 2D-2 for column-type forms. Occupancy pair entry: the freeness form of the r-parameter lift fails on the board at r = 2 for occupancy pairs with Q = 2D-2; a 5-row restriction of the pair is refuted at degree 3, so at D = 3 the conjecture needs t >= 6 or Q >= 5 (calibration, not a refutation). Sub-board refutations entry: at D = 3 it needs t >= 8 or Q >= 5; a 7-row locally infeasible robust pair is refuted at degree 3. Product-constraints entry: a bounded-r, p=3 analogue under fullness and label robustness; not a proof.

claims.summary: Component hypothesis: for forbid-value constraints on the weak unary base over F_3, grouped into components along bounded circuits and each component replaced by a degree-compatible basis of its pattern ideal I(P_C), with (p-1) d_C + 2 w_C <= D and local freeness (the map gr R_C -> A injective through D), every syzygy of the leading forms in A through degree D is generated by Koszul, Frobenius and component-local syzygies. A first formulation without local freeness is false (narrow form x_11 + x_21 forbidding 0).

Supported only by model and board data of small size; the logarithmic-prefix images are not forbid-value products.

formalization.scope: Informal finite computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: States the genericity input the core statement's inductive step needs, and the conditions under which it would exclude refutations.

claims.summary: Pencil splitting identity: for the degree-k multiplication pencil G(w) = G_a + w G_b of two forms on the weak unary PHP top algebra A (A_(k-1) -> A_k, N = gamma_k), the number of right minimal indices eps_i = 0 equals dim(A/(l_a, l_b))_k; the right kernel sheaf on P^1 splits as sum O(-eps_i) (Forney) with rank N - rho and degree -(rho - sum eta - k_reg). So freeness in degree k is the count of trivial summands matching HS_A/(1+t+t^2)^2, and a non-pointwise defect is a change in splitting type at fixed rank and degree. At n = 8, degree 3: occupancy pair (19685, 1525, 64) summands O, O(-1), O(-2) against random pairs (19682, 1531, 61).

claims.summary: First-degree lift: in the matching complex over a field of characteristic 3, for r row-linear forms of width at least r+3 (every nonzero combination nonconstant on r+3 rows) that are (r+1)(r+2)-robust (each row's evaluation matrix 1, f^(1..r) keeps its rank after deleting that many labels), every symmetric tuple in K_1 is a polarized lift (D^a w)_{|a|=2} of some w in K_3. Proof by tensors of short pieces: the joint kernel of all D_j in K_1 is spanned by elements on at most r+1 rows and (r+1)^2 labels, each lifted with its own inserted vectors on two further rows; mixed moments are realized because products of three evaluations from distinct rows span cubic forms.
claims.assessment: Working proof with no exactness hypothesis; exact GF(3) check at r = 3 (lifting holds exactly at width >= 4 on 44 small boards, and at full dimension on two boards meeting the hypotheses). Width r+3 is sufficient, not sharp.

formalization.scope: Informal proof; exact GF(3) finite check at r = 3 only; no Lean verification.

claims.summary: Peeling locality: over any field, for subspaces P_i = P of k^r common to all rows, the joint kernel T_t of the contractions on square-free degree-t tensors (+)_{|S|=t} (x)_{i in S} P_i is spanned by elements on at most 2t rows, for every t and number of rows. claims.summary: Row Horace identity: on the functional matching complex, for a row i, K_t = K'_t (+) K^{ni i}_t and D_l = D'_l + partial_l; the double-point space Z = {w in K_3 : D_l^2 w = 0 for all l} equals {w0 + w1 : w1 in Z_res, T w0 = -C w1} with T the trace problem on the board without row i, Z_res = {w1 : D'^2_l w1 = 0} and coupling C = (partial D' + D' partial); so dim Z = dim ker T + dim Z_res - rank(Z_res -> coker T). claims.summary: Edge Castelnuovo sequence: for a bipartite board Gamma (top algebra G(Gamma) = edge variables modulo row/label collisions, squares and row sums) and an edge e=(i,a), over any field G(Gamma)/(x_e) = G(Gamma minus e) and multiplication by x_e factors through a surjection G_{t-1}(Gamma/e) -> x_e G_{t-1}(Gamma) (Gamma/e deletes row i and label a); if the matching complex of Gamma minus e restricted to every t-set of rows containing i has no reduced homology in degree t-2, then 0 -> G_{t-1}(Gamma/e) -> G_t(Gamma) -> G_t(Gamma minus e) -> 0 is exact. Proof: the deletion-link sequence in top degree, extending link cycles by coning. The analogue of the Castelnuovo sequence of the Horace method, with degree drop in the residual.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: An exact deletion-contraction tool for the double-point problem on matching complexes of arbitrary bipartite boards.
significance.next_action: Use in a differential Horace degeneration over several rows, or in the route review of the double-point line.

claims.summary: No Horace balancing: on the PHP board (R=n+1, N=n) in characteristic 3, for the row split and (given exactness of the edge sequence in degree 3) every edge split, the trace problem is overdetermined at the total capacity; for edges this is equivalent to dim G_2(Gamma/e) > gamma_3/(gamma_1-1), true for n=6..10 (165..2475 against 48.4..806.5) and for all n>=4 given the dimension formula (2n^4-10n^3+7n^2+23n-29>0). Trace-free means the trace part squares to zero. Forms whose trace part squares to zero impose at most (R-1)(N-1)-1 (row split) or gamma_1(Gamma/e)-1 (edge split) conditions, fewer than gamma_1-1, so the Alexander-Hirschowitz balancing by points off the hyperplane has no analogue below capacity, and every argument by these splits must control a coupling.
claims.assessment: Working proof (general inequalities) with the numerical comparison for n=6..10 from exact dimensions; the all-n edge comparison uses the dimension formula.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Shows the double-point proof by Horace splits is always in the differential case.
significance.next_action: Route review of the double-point line.

claims.summary: Quiet members: over F_p, if P in F_p^d is the common zero set of m clauses prod_{j in S_b} L_{b,j}(y)^{p-1} with |S_b|=k <= d affine forms of linearly independent linear parts, then every nonzero reduced polynomial of total degree r vanishing on P satisfies p^{-r/(p-1)} <= m(1-1/p)^k (union bound plus the generalized Reed-Muller minimum weight). At the logarithmic-prefix reduction's parameters (k = ceil((K+1) log n / log(p/(p-1))), at most n^K clauses) m(1-1/p)^k <= 1/n, so a member's local reduction (the functions on its span vanishing on P) has no nonzero element of reduced y-degree below (p-1) log_p n. It bounds y-degree only, over the abstract F_p^d, for clauses of k independent forms.
claims.assessment: Working proof after a record check and a fresh-context review; checked exactly on 189 random families.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Budget-respecting adversarial members cannot create constant-degree local falls; the width-1 phenomena that did (pencils, pinned spans) lie outside the budget.
significance.next_action: Improve the exponent to order k for the reduction's product-structured families, or construct a budget family at the current bound.

claims.summary: Tropical leading bound: for forms with coefficients c_{j,x} t^{w_j(x)} (generic c, integer weights) on the pattern algebra (any monomial algebra of faces), the double-point rank of generic forms over F_3bar is at least the rank of the leading matrix A_0 (each 3-face row keeps its terms of minimal t-order w_j(F) - w_j(u)); for tie-free weights A_0 has one nonzero per row, at (winning form, its heaviest cell), and its rank is the number of distinct such pairs, which is at most M(gamma_1-2) because a form's two lightest cells are never the heaviest cell of a 3-face; so tie-free weights never certify maximal rank min(gamma_3, M(gamma_1-1)) at M <= capacity, and ties are necessary.
claims.assessment: Working proof (row scaling and semicontinuity; the simplest case of Draisma's tropical approach to secant dimensions).

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: A certified combinatorial lower bound that uses the monomial structure of the degenerate algebra, candidate mechanism for all-n maximal rank.
significance.next_action: Design tied weights whose leading blocks have provable rank.

claims.summary: Kunneth component locality: over F_3, let G be a graded commutative algebra with l^3 = 0 on G_1, and linear forms U = U_1 + ... + U_m whose spans W_i form a direct sum W; with T_i = Sym(W_i)/(cubes), T = Sym(W)/(cubes) = tensor of T_i, A_i = F_3[x_j : j in U_i]/(x_j^3), A = tensor of A_i acting by x_j -> l_j, and any homogeneous J_i in A_i, J = sum J_i A: if G is free through degree B over T (a T-linear map T (x) C -> G bijective in degrees <= B), then Tor_1^A(A/J, G)_s = [sum_i Tor_1^{A_i}(A_i/J_i, T_i) (x) prod_{k != i} T_k/J_k T_k (x) C]_s for s <= B, so every syzygy of the chosen generators of J (the union of generating sets of the J_i) is generated by G-combinations of A-syzygies (Frobenius, Koszul for selectors) and syzygies supported on one component; forms within a component may be dependent. This proves the syzygy conclusion of conj:component-hypothesis for components with independent spans under joint freeness.
claims.assessment: Working proof (truncation, freeness and the Kunneth formula over a field) after a fresh-context review.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Proves the component hypothesis's syzygy conclusion in the independent-span regime; isolates freeness and span dependence as what remains for adversarial inventories.
significance.next_action: State and test a freeness condition for spans in terms of Q-robustness.

claims.summary: Degreewise gluing: for U, W in the Boolean cube over any field, degree-d functions on U and W agreeing on U n W glue to a degree-d function on U u W iff I_d(U n W) = I_d(U) + I_d(W) iff dim F_d(UuW) - dim F_d(U) - dim F_d(W) + dim F_d(UnW) = 0 (always <= 0); this holds for all d <= D iff the graded Mayer-Vietoris sequence of graded function modules is exact through D. claims.summary: Leaf reduction: over F_3 (also F_q), for a family F of systems (ideals in their private variables and the shared coordinates they read, pairwise disjoint private variables, no cross generators) and a system a reading exactly one shared coordinate x, with U any set of other systems, R = F \ a, and M_U, M_W the top ideals of U and R \ U in the truncated algebra A_R of x and R's variables: if x^alpha A_R cap (M_U + M_W) = (x^alpha A_R cap M_U) + x^alpha M_W for alpha = 1, 2 (a modular law over the chain ring F_3[x]/(x^3); it fails even for ideals, e.g. A_R = S[y]/(y^3), M_U = (x+y), M_W = (y)), then every degree at which F falls (in the family's algebra) is one at which {a} cup U or R falls. Proof: A = A_a tensor_S A_R with an adapted basis for n_a; the law splits N_a cap N_R into N_a cap N_U plus N_a N_W, whose Koszul syzygies lift exactly. Consequence: a path a-b-c-d without cross generators satisfying the law when peeling a (U = {b}) and then b in {b,c,d} (U = {c}) has lowest fall equal to the least over its three linked pairs. Separately, a four-block path of ENS blocks at h = 4 with R on its links (outside the lemma) has no fall below 8 (exact).

claims.summary: Occupancy-pinned PHP (conjecture): over F_3 there are c > 0 and, for each n, some e <= n/2 with e = 2 (mod 3) such that weak unary PHP^{n+1}_n plus the pins C_j = 0 (j <= e) and C_j = 1 (j > e) has no PC refutation of degree n^c. The pinned system is an onto weak PHP (rows sum to 1 mod 3, each remaining hole exactly one pigeon) of n+1 pigeons into n-e holes with counts agreeing mod 3; e not = 2 (mod 3) is refuted at degree 1 by counting. It is implied by a PC lower bound for Beame-Riis onto functional PHP^{N+3^l}_N over F_3 (listed open in their 1998 paper), and it transfers their Nullstellensatz bound: NS coefficient degree >= 2l-1 (about 1.37 log_3 n, a constant factor below the needed 4(K+1) log_3 n) when e+1 = 3^l and n-e >= (5^l - 3^l)/2; their Lemma 8.7 refutes their system at NS degree 3^l - 1, so this route needs e+1 = 3^l above the target degree. The reduction needs only degree O(log n); n^c is a stronger form. Mikša-Nordström's onto PHP (pigeon clauses) does not cover the mod-3 linear rows.
claims.assessment: Proved for n >= 5 with e = 2 and c = 1/3 by cor:column-statistic-families-random-prefix (restriction to onto weak PHP and thm:spare-pigeon-onto-hardness); degree bound ceil((n-2)/2)+1.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Its truth would take column statistics out of W_RS's heavy core.
significance.next_action: Search post-1998 literature for PC lower bounds on onto functional PHP with counts congruent mod p; otherwise attempt an Alekhnovich-Razborov argument on an unbalanced expander.

claims.summary: Subflat obstruction: over F_p, p odd, replace each Res(Lin_Fp) line's falsifying set {f_i != a_i} by kept value sets {f_i in T_i}, T_i a nonempty subset of F_p minus a_i. For single-literal lines f = a, g = b whose forms take every value pair on the allowed points and their resolvent alpha f + beta g = alpha a + beta b (alpha, beta != 0, kept set T), the weakened step is sound only if |T_f| + |T_g| >= p - 1 + |T| >= p (Cauchy-Davenport on alpha A + beta B, A, B the complements); at p = 3 one premise keeps its whole falsifying set on the resolved literal, and one flat per line is never sound at such a step, whatever rule picks the values; at p = 2 the kept set is the whole falsifying set. Side literals need the value-pair hypothesis jointly; literals on single variables fail it.

claims.summary: Dance shared patterns: over F_3, for a W_RS block with forms L_k (coefficients a_{k,u}) and a pigeon i, call holes c, c' equivalent if a_{k,(i,c)} = a_{k,(i,c')} for all k. Equivalent holes give one-pigeon extensions rho+(i,c), rho+(i,c') the same zero pattern at every partial matching rho, so one killed pattern removes a whole class; inequivalent holes are separated at some rho under a value hypothesis on the separating form (assumed, not verified in general). All holes equivalent for every pigeon iff the forms lie in the span of the row sums and constants; then each clause is a polynomial f(r) of degree <= 4t+2 in the row sums and lies in C_{4t+2}(R) unless the pattern gamma* at r = 1 is killed (probability <= 3^{-t}), so designs of the row equations vanish on it though not supported in the allowed set (a formal analogue of the record's normal-form reduction, not a case of it). The naive pigeon dance inside Q therefore fails through coefficient classes; certificates must be taken modulo the row equations.

claims.summary: Defect decay: in prop:lift-obstruction's setting with product tops and lifted Frobenius elements, let W_0(R) be the syzygies z with every Phi_{b,j}(z) in I_R. claims.summary: Class survival: over F_3, in prop:lift-obstruction's setting with product tops and lifted Frobenius elements, let R have zero defect below e and R^+ be any extension by columns with arbitrary coefficients. Then the classes Syz_e(R^+)/T_e(R^+) embed into Q = Syz_e(R)/T_e(R) by restriction (lower degrees stay clean), and a nonzero surviving class x has every added cell's coefficient vector in K_0(x) = {kappa : sum kappa Phi(x) in I_R}; if x is not in W_0(R)/T_e(R), some nonzero combination of the forms of the tops in S(x) = {b : some Phi_{b,j}(x) not in I_R} vanishes on every added cell. Hence Def_e(R^+) = 0 if W_0(R) = T_e(R) and for every nonzero class x the forms of S(x) are independent on the added cells, deterministically. The defect-1 pair of cor:defect-decay has zero 2h+1 defect on every extension where its four forms are independent off the base.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: First adversary-proof mechanism on A1's dense core: surviving non-Taylor classes force sparse relations among the forms of their tops.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

claims.summary: Characteristic 0, N >= 6: (1) the closure in M_(0,N)-bar of the configurations with a Moebius involution inducing pi lies in Fix(pi); (2) at a point with smooth spine of a caterpillar-tailed F-curve of type (a,b,c,d), a pi in whose fixed locus it lies has at least mu(a,b,c,d) fixed marks (mu from the tail-permutation rules, phi(1) = 1, phi(k) = k-2); (3) every total caterpillar lies in the closure of Sym_pi for its reversal pi, which is weighted (a non-branch fixed point of weight >= m(m-1)/2 >= 3), hence in the closure of the weight-three locus; (4) a caterpillar-tailed type with at least two size-one tails has a total caterpillar among its special points, so the boundary-curve criterion's hypothesis fails for every curve (1,1,m,N-2-m); types with at most one single mark have no chain special point. Interior-clean families still span for 8 <= N <= 400 (finite check), but interior cleanness does not give the hypothesis.
claims.assessment: Working proof: fixed loci are closed; automorphisms of stable curves preserve the dual tree and are the identity on three-pointed components with three fixed special points; mirror-symmetric degenerations sigma(z) = -z with hierarchical clusters at +-1 realize every total caterpillar; the chain/non-chain dichotomy of the spine collisions. Interior spanning is a finite check (research/tools/bmd_cube_fcurve_symclean.gp).

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Refutes the boundary-curve criterion's hypothesis for the family (1,1,m,N-2-m) through symmetry at special points, and shows which types remain possible.

claims.summary: Characteristic 0, at fixed distinct cluster shapes (generic points of boundary strata, not F-curve points), clusters of sizes n_1..n_4 collapsing at distinct points p_i (branch points p_i + eps b^(i)_j, each cluster space of weight 0 at its mark when n_i >= 3): as eps -> 0 at fixed z, (1) the empty-pattern class (1, z, pairs inside clusters) tends to H^0(P^1, O(infinity + sum_i C_i p_i)), C_i = binom(n_i,2); (2) single-single classes are unchanged, and a class joining a single to cluster i tends to ((z-p_i)(z-p_i'))^(1/2) Pol_(<n_i)((z-p_i)^(-1)); (3) for n_i, n_i' >= 2 the leading terms of the class {i,i'} span ((z-p_i)(z-p_i'))^(1/2) times the rational functions with poles of order < n_i at p_i, < n_i' at p_i', bounded at infinity, of dimension n_i + n_i' - 1, so (n_i - 1)(n_i' - 1) dimensions of the limit come from higher orders (a two-cluster neck).
claims.assessment: Working proof: monodromy classes, ordinary frames of the cluster spaces at their marks, Vandermonde for binomial series, partial fractions and Riemann-Roch on P^1. Analogue of lem:cube-cross-block-defect; the deficits agree at n_i = n_i' = 2.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Shows that the spines of fully symmetry-clean boundary curves contain two-cluster neck problems; whether window methods apply is open.

claims.summary: Characteristic 0, N >= 5. For S of size k and generic separated b, the curve C_S in M_{0,N}-bar traced by translating the points of S rigidly (a_i = b_i + s, i in S) is complete, meets the boundary only at the k(N-k) pair collisions (general points of Delta_{ij}) and, for 2 <= k <= N-2, at s = infinity (a general point of Delta_S); C_S . B_j = 0 for j >= 3, j != min(k,N-k), and is positive for j = 2 and j = min(k,N-k) >= 3, so C_1, C_3, ..., C_{floor(N/2)} have spanning S_N-symmetrized classes. At each boundary point the limit of V_a is unique on each component: a basis holomorphic in the chart and in z (away from marks and nodes) has independent value there. Hence codim W_3 >= 2, and so (K), holds at N if these curves satisfy interior (no weight >= 3 non-branch point, also at s = infinity for k = 1), boundary (no such point in the unique limits) and escape (no weight-3 points converging to marks, branch points or nodes) conditions.
claims.assessment: Working proof: boundary structure of rigid translation, positivity of local intersection multiplicities, triangular pairing with the Keel-McKernan basis B_j, valuation reduction over the generic point of each divisor giving a holomorphic basis with independent restriction on a dense open subset, and the criterion's item (3) with curve selection and semicontinuity. The three conditions are unproved for every N; at N = 6 at least one of C_1, C_3 must fail a condition (involution divisor).

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: A spanning family for the boundary-curve criterion with unique limits, for every N, replacing the F-curve family whose spine limits are arc-dependent.

claims.summary: For every e, l >= 1, the Wronskian of the far space F_k of the base peeling degeneration (c = 1), with its factors x and 1+x removed, is a polynomial W_k irreducible over Q of degree #F_k = 4l(2e^2+6el-5e-4l+5). Irreducibility implies W_k squarefree, one of the two statements to which the peeling reduction derives the base weight bound (B) for even N.
claims.assessment: Conjecture. Verified exactly over Q at (e,l) = (1,1), (1,2), (2,1), (2,2) (research/tools/bmd_cube_far_wronskian.gp; research/results/bmd-20260930-zzm/far-wronskians.txt), which proves squarefreeness there. Two alternative mechanisms are refuted by the same data: W_k does not split over Q into lower-degree (e.g. classical) factors, and at least half its roots are non-real and the real ones are not confined to one interval, so orthogonality for a positive measure on the real line does not apply (non-Hermitian orthogonality is not excluded). Squarefreeness mod 2^61-1 for b <= 6 was already known (check:cube-peeling-far-components); irreducibility over Q is new.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: An arithmetic mechanism for the far half of (B).
